messages:
morgan: Heads-up — planning an RBAC change in the private deploy that tightens the service account perms for the onprem logship agent. before we roll: need signoff on KMS access pattern + a vuln question about the agent binary. short thread, pls react.

samir: Can you paste the new RoleBinding? main concern is we don't accidentally give the logship SA Decrypt on the primary key. ideally it should have only Encrypt/EncryptVerify for wrapping.

morgan: paste: ```yaml
kind: Role
metadata: {name: logship-writer}
rules:
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["pods/log"]
    verbs: ["get", "list", "watch"]
---
kind: RoleBinding
metadata: {name: logship-writer-binding}
subjects: [{kind: ServiceAccount, name: logship-sa, namespace: infra-priv}]
roleRef: {kind: Role, name: logship-writer}
```
we're also switching the agent from a shared KMS key to a dedicated envelope key per-customer.

anya: SGTM but we need to update the agent config so it never calls kms:Decrypt directly from the node. use envelope flow — agent encrypts locally with a data key, then calls KMS to wrap/unwrap the data key only. update config like: ```yaml
logship:
  envelope: true
  kms_key_id: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/priv/cryptoKeys/logship-wrap
  rotate_interval: 168h
```
and add audit_log: true.

lee: quick FYI — vuln scan flagged lib-transport v0.9.3 in the logship agent (CVE-2024-9999). fix available in v0.9.5 but upstream change touches the transport handshake. i'd prefer we block the agent upgrade until we can test canary. for immediate mitigation: apply pod NetworkPolicy to disallow egress except to our KMS host and SIEM collectors. also add an iptables rule on the node to drop unexpected outbound.

sec-bot: automated-alert: ticket #SEC-4821 created for CVE-2024-9999 in infra-priv/logship-agent. severity: HIGH. added to "private-deploy-vuln-triage" board.

morgan: thanks. proposed rollout plan: 1) apply RBAC change + new RoleBinding in infra-priv (dry-run cluster A) 2) patch agent config to envelope mode, enable audit_log 3) deploy agent v0.9.4 to canary nodes (not full 0.9.5 until handshake test) 4) enforce NetworkPolicy egress allowlist to kms+siem 5) run key rotation sim and confirm logs still decryptable by ops-runner 6) promote.

samir: checklist item: ensure KMS role for logship-sa is limited to `wrap/unwrap` and `getPublicKey` only. no key:decrypt. also add a KMS IAM condition: `request.auth.claims.namespace == "infra-priv"` if supported.

anya: add to checklist: update audit forwarding so we ship raw audit events to the SIEM and a hashed-only stream to the hosted analytics (to avoid any accidental PII leakage). and test retention/ttl config.

lee: incident-runbook notes — if CVE exploit observed, isolate node, rotate envelope keys, revoke logship SA tokens, and failover collectors to read-only mode. i've linked the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/private-logship-incident (see steps 2/3/4).

morgan: sounds good. do we have ops bandwidth to run the canary this week? if so i'll schedule and create the PRs. pls :thumbsup: if you're OK.

ops-bot: scheduled canary window requested: 2024-04-12 02:00-04:00 UTC. pinging oncall.

samir: :thumbsup: will validate KMS IAM and run the key-rotation sim in my sandbox.

anya: :thumbsup: i'll prepare audit-forwarding test prompts and verify no plaintext leaks.

lee: i'll craft the NetworkPolicy manifest and the temporary iptables rollback script.

morgan: thanks all — i'll open the RBAC + config PRs and link SEC-4821. will update thread once PRs are up.
